cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Acknowledge Our History
cards.instruction: Make someone recognize that the relationship, memory, or sacrifice mattered and cannot be treated as incidental.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you bin our ferry ticket, remember the overtime we worked for that weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We missed the ferry. I hate being reminded.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. We stayed anyway. That was the first time we chose each other over a refund.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keep the hotel receipt, then. That part was lovely.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you write that on the envelope? In your handwriting, so it isn't just me saying it mattered.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 commands remembrance, but A3 narrative and A5 will you write are ordinary emotional appeals after detachable high-status phrases.

relationship.evidence: B2 dislikes a failure reminder and B4 offers a positive keepsake, making the partner helpful and specific.

heightening.evidence: B4 lovely hotel memory causes A5 to seek B handwriting as evidence that meaning is shared.

specificity.evidence: A1 overtime and ferry ticket establish sacrifice; A3 stay and B4 hotel make the replacement memory coherent.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 not just me saying it mattered is sincere and earned, but the generic rank prefix jars with the tactic.
